name: Teatro Real

position.source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/4328975 (centroid of the outline; long axis at 92.0°, the Plaza de Oriente front faces 272°)

rights.note: Designed by Antonio López Aguado (from 1818), finished by Custodio Teodoro Moreno and opened in 1850: the 19th-century façades are in the public domain. The 1988–1997 refurbishment (José Manuel González-Valcárcel, who died in 1992, then Francisco Rodríguez de Partearroyo; the stage block led by Jaime González-Valcárcel) rebuilt the roofs and the stage tower, which are most of what is seen from the air and are still protected — hence «protected» for the whole.

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q211250_teatro_real.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. Plan from OpenStreetMap: the elongated hexagon of the outer range (walls to 26 m, a rounded lead roof whose crest reaches the OSM 30 m, computed across the varying width of the range), the inner block with a flat roof at 27 m and a few plant rooms, the auditorium roof (low gable, 31 m), the stage tower (walls 35 m, gabled to 40 m, ridge east–west as OSM says, a raised strip along it to 42 m) and the arcaded porch on the Plaza de Oriente (9.5 m, carrying the balcony); the west front follows the shallow concave arc of the OSM outline. Elevations measured on near-frontal photos (±5 %): granite ground storey to 9.5 m, main floor to 17.5 m, cornice 26 m; an attic colonnade on the east and side fronts, large windows between pilasters and a balustrade on the west front. Stylised: windows with flat pediments and balconies, 8-sided columns, oculi, pilasters and the big arched windows of the stage-tower gables; window counts are approximate. Uncertain: the exact profile of the curved roofs, the height of the stage-tower walls (35 m, from the OSM roof height) and the plant rooms on the inner roof (placed by eye).
